phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Abstract Interpretation Analysis of multiply_polynomialcoeff (SG-009): Degree Bounds Verification

input_variables.name: a
constraints: len(a) represents degree + 1 in coefficient form
Each element in BLS12-381 scalar field

input_variables.name: b
constraints: len(b) represents degree + 1 in coefficient form
Each element in BLS12-381 scalar field

input_variables.name: FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB
input_variables.notes: Global constant defining maximum polynomial degree for extended blob domain

intermediate_variables.name: r
intermediate_variables.length_evolution: grows from 1 to at most len(a) + len(b) - 1
intermediate_variables.degree_evolution: deg(r) increases up to deg(a) + deg(b)

intermediate_variables.name: power
intermediate_variables.purpose: Loop iteration index over coefficients of polynomial a

intermediate_variables.name: coef
intermediate_variables.purpose: Current coefficient from polynomial a at position 'power'

output_variable.name: r
post_conditions: r represents polynomial product a(x) * b(x)

abstract_operations_trace.precondition: a and b are valid PolynomialCoeff objects
abstract_operations_trace.purpose: Ensure product polynomial degree stays within trusted setup bounds

abstract_operations_trace.abstract_transform: r.degree := -∞ (or conceptually 0 for zero polynomial), r.length := 1
abstract_operations_trace.state: r initialized as additive identity for polynomial addition

loop_invariant: After iteration i: r accumulates sum of a[j]*b(x)*x^j for j ∈ [0, i]
deg(r) after iteration i: at most i + deg(b)

abstract_operations_trace.operation: summand = [0]*power + [coef * x for x in b]
abstract_operations_trace.degree_analysis: Each summand has degree power + deg(b)

abstract_operations_trace.accumulation: r accumulates terms from polynomial multiplication via distributive property

final_state.r.degree: max over all iterations of (power + deg(b)) = (len(a) - 1) + deg(b) = deg(a) + deg(b)

abstract_operations_trace.postcondition_check: deg(r) = deg(a) + deg(b) <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB - 2 (from step 1 assertion)

state_anomalies_found.description: Missing or incorrect assertion check for polynomial degree bounds

abstract_state.precondition: Implementation lacks assertion: len(a) + len(b) <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB
abstract_state.result: Product polynomial degree exceeds trusted setup domain

reachability.attacker_control: Malicious peer provides crafted missing cell indices causing large vanishing polynomial

impact.cryptographic: KZG commitment computed with insufficient trusted setup points
impact.security: Proofs become verifiable but potentially exploitable due to under-constrained polynomial space

state_anomalies_found.test_trigger: 1. Craft polynomial a with len(a) = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 + 10. 2. Craft polynomial b with len(b) = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 + 10. 3. Call multiply_polynomialcoeff(a, b). 4. Verify assertion fires (expected) or product is computed (vulnerability).

formal_specification.required_precondition: ∀ a, b ∈ PolynomialCoeff: len(a) + len(b) ≤ FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB

state_anomalies_found.description: Incorrect assertion boundary: using < instead of <=, or vice versa
state_anomalies_found.impact: If assertion is too strict (<), valid polynomial multiplications are rejected. If too loose (+ 1), invalid large polynomials are accepted.
state_anomalies_found.test_trigger: Test with len(a) + len(b) = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB exactly and verify acceptance.

state_anomalies_found.description: Summand length calculation overflow in degenerate cases

abstract_state.overflow_condition: If assertion is bypassed, summand length could exceed language max list size

state_anomalies_found.reachability: Only reachable if SA-001 (assertion bypass) exists
state_anomalies_found.impact: Memory allocation failure, crash, or undefined behavior in list construction
state_anomalies_found.mitigation: Step 1 assertion prevents this by bounding len(a) + len(b)

state_anomalies_found.description: Final polynomial degree does not match expected deg(a) + deg(b)

anomalous_cases.condition: If highest-degree terms in summands cancel during addition
anomalous_cases.probability: Negligible in BLS12-381 field (requires exact coefficient match)

anomalous_cases.validity: Mathematically correct, but may violate type assumptions

state_anomalies_found.impact: Violation of INV-002 could cause downstream failures in KZG proof generation
state_anomalies_found.test_trigger: 1. Test with a = [0], b = [1, 2]. 2. Test with non-zero inputs and verify deg(result) = deg(a) + deg(b).

state_anomalies_found.description: Product polynomial degree exceeds KZG trusted setup domain size

abstract_state.consequence: g1_lincomb(KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, poly) accesses out-of-bounds trusted setup points

attack_scenario.attacker_action: Provide malicious cell indices causing large vanishing polynomial in construct_vanishing_polynomial (SG-022)
attack_scenario.exploit: If SG-009 lacks assertion, iterative multiplication in SG-012 produces polynomial with deg > FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB - 1
attack_scenario.result: Commitment computation uses non-existent trusted setup points, producing invalid but parseable proof

impact.consequence: Attacker can craft proofs that pass verification but violate polynomial commitment security assumptions

state_anomalies_found.test_trigger: Test procedure from property PROP-W3B4-15: 1. Locate multiply_polynomialcoeff. 2. Verify assertion exists. 3. Craft inputs len(a) = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 + 100, len(b) = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 + 100. 4. Verify rejection.

state_anomalies_found.description: Numerical instability or incorrect accumulation in add_polynomialcoeff

abstract_state.concern: If add_polynomialcoeff has bugs (e.g., incorrect zero-padding), final result incorrect

state_anomalies_found.impact: Incorrect polynomial product coefficients, causing wrong KZG proofs
state_anomalies_found.mitigation: Relies on correctness of SG-008; not a direct multiply_polynomialcoeff issue

trust_boundary_analysis.name: Polynomial Engine → Proof Generator
trust_boundary_analysis.description: multiply_polynomialcoeff sits at trust boundary between polynomial arithmetic (untrusted attacker-influenced inputs) and cryptographic proof generation (trusted setup assumptions)
input_sources: P2P network: cells from remote peers during recovery
Vanishing polynomial construction: depends on missing cell indices (attacker-controlled)
trust_boundary_analysis.output_consumer: KZG proof generation (g1_lincomb with trusted setup)

boundary_enforcement.purpose: Enforce polynomial degree stays within trusted setup bounds
boundary_enforcement.consequence_of_failure: Trusted setup assumptions violated, cryptographic soundness compromised

attack_surface.vector: Malicious P2P peer provides crafted cells or cell indices
attack_surface.amplification: SG-012 (vanishing_polynomialcoeff) calls SG-009 in loop, potentially building large polynomial iteratively
attack_surface.detection: Assertion at SG-009 entry catches violations before propagation

verification_strategy.approach: Property-based testing with abstract domain constraints
key_properties: ∀ a, b: len(a) + len(b) > FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB ⇒ multiply_polynomialcoeff(a, b) raises AssertionError
∀ a, b: len(a) + len(b) ≤ FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB ⇒ deg(result) = deg(a) + deg(b)
∀ a, b: len(a) + len(b) ≤ FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB ⇒ len(result) = len(a) + len(b) - 1

test_cases.expected: deg(result) = 3, len(result) = 4, coefficients match convolution of inputs

test_cases.setup: Construct vanishing polynomial for many missing cells (large xs list)
test_cases.action: Call vanishing_polynomialcoeff(xs) which iteratively calls multiply_polynomialcoeff
test_cases.expected: If len(xs) is large, intermediate multiplications must respect degree bound

symbolic_execution_targets: Loop invariant: deg(r) after iteration i = i + deg(b)

invariants: INV-002: deg(result) = deg(a) + deg(b) (from SG-009 graph)

implementation_search_notes.context: This audit is based on the Ethereum Fulu specification (https://ethereum.github.io/consensus-specs/specs/fulu/polynomial-commitments-sampling/)
